title: How much land does each person end up with?
description: A road takes one sixth of a piece of land, and the rest is shared. The land each person gets is found by multiplying fractions of the land that remains.
teaching_notes: One idea: a share of the remaining land is a fraction of that remainder, not of the whole land, so we multiply the two fractions. Watch for students who take the shares as fractions of the original land.

video_script.why: The child uses the multiply method of the solved example on shares of land that remains after a road.
video_script.substitution: the book's own question, one sixth of the land taken, then half and one third of the rest given away
video_script.anchor: a plot of land with one sixth cut off for a road and the rest to be shared
video_script.payoff_line: Ruhee keeps five thirty sixths of the original land

final_answer.spoken: five thirty sixths of the original land

video_script.fraction_reading: one sixth, five sixths, one half, one third, five twelfths, five eighteenths, five thirty sixths

names.Ruhee: has land, one sixth of which is taken for a road
names.Jia: the daughter, given half of the remaining land
names.Laksh: the son, given a third of the remaining land

maths_rules: (c) the part of the remaining land left = 1 − 1/2 − 1/3 = 6/6 − 3/6 − 2/6 = 1/6, and 1/6 × 5/6 = 5/36
video_script.design: A plot with one sixth cut off. The rest is a bar that is cut into shares; every product is a fraction of that rest.
open_questions: The worklist works (c) by subtracting 5/6 − 5/12 − 5/18; this script finds the share left over first and multiplies, which gives the same 5/36.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about sharing land.
<bookmark mark='road'/>The government takes one sixth of Ruhee's land for a road.
<bookmark mark='share'/>Half of the rest goes to Ruhee's daughter Jia, and a third goes to Ruhee's son Laksh.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What part of the original land does each get, and what part does Ruhee keep?

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>We use the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='of'/>A share of the rest is a fraction of the remaining land, so we multiply.
<bookmark mark='look'/>Before multiplying, we look for a top and a bottom with a common factor.

beats.on_screen: Given: road takes 1/6; Jia gets 1/2 of the rest; Laksh gets 1/3 of the rest

marks.kids: the two shares are written beside the road

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the road takes one sixth, and then the rest is shared.
<bookmark mark='kids'/>Jia gets one half of the rest, and Laksh gets one third of it.

beats.on_screen: To find: the land that remains; the part each of Jia, Laksh and Ruhee gets

marks.find: the words To find and the four questions are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the land that remains, and the part each person gets.

marks.one: the whole is written as six sixths

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, the land left after the road is one minus one sixth.
<bookmark mark='take'/>Writing one as six sixths, six sixths minus one sixth is five sixths.

marks.a: the first share is written as a product of one half and five sixths
marks.b: the second share is written as a product of one third and five sixths

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step two, Jia gets one half of five sixths. That is one times five over two times six, or five twelfths.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Laksh gets one third of five sixths. That is one times five over three times six, or five eighteenths.

beats.on_screen: left for Ruhee = 1 − 1/2 − 1/3 = 6/6 − 3/6 − 2/6 = 1/6 of the remaining land

marks.left: the part of the remaining land left is written as one minus two fractions
marks.sixths: each fraction is rewritten in sixths

narration: <bookmark mark='left'/>Step three, find the part of the remaining land left for Ruhee. That is one minus one half minus one third.
<bookmark mark='sixths'/>In sixths, six sixths minus three sixths minus two sixths leaves one sixth.

beats.on_screen: Ruhee keeps 1/6 × 5/6 = (1 × 5)/(6 × 6) of the original land

marks.keep: the share kept is written as a product of one sixth and five sixths
marks.tops: the tops and the bottoms are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='keep'/>Step four, Ruhee keeps one sixth of the five sixths.
<bookmark mark='tops'/>That is one times five over six times six.

marks.given: the two gifts are added in thirty sixths
marks.less: the sum is compared with the land that remained

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Step five, check that the two gifts together are less than the five sixths.
<bookmark mark='less'/>Fifteen plus ten thirty sixths is twenty five thirty sixths. That is less than thirty thirty sixths.

beats.on_screen: Answer: remains 5/6; (a) Jia gets 5/12; (b) Laksh gets 5/18; (c) Ruhee keeps 5/36 of the original land

marks.keep: the share Ruhee keeps is boxed last

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Five sixths of the land remains. Jia gets five twelfths, and Laksh gets five eighteenths.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>Ruhee keeps five thirty sixths of the original land.
